title: Problem-Solving: Take the Lead
coreMove: Lead the process of solving together without taking ownership of the solution away from the other person.
sourcePressure: The chapter shifts into design only when ready, avoiding drift and unilateral prescription through joint inquiry, options, standards, and specific agency-matched commitments.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Jumping to fix the issue before understanding and expression have happened.

sourceAnchors.name: joint inquiry into solutions
sourceAnchors.detail: The source tells the speaker to lead the process by proposing joint inquiry, inventing options, using mutual standards, and specifying next steps.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Taking the lead means protecting the process from drift, not grabbing the steering wheel from the other person.

sourceAnchorsNote: No chapter-specific real named anecdote, study, or researcher was available in the source sidecars for this chapter. Source anchors are traceable framework artifacts or edition/context facts only; do not invent named studies or reuse the source-banned Jack-Michael, Sydney, or author-family examples.
